reader.decision: Approve both guards (scheduler dedupe and the renewal_charges NOT EXISTS check), but first have the scheduler guard's logic corrected/clarified as noted in follow-ups. Do not block the charge guard; ship it now.
reader.decision_reason: The message gives a coherent cause (repeated 02:30 local hour, no idempotency, renews_on advanced only in settle) and the two guards cover distinct failure modes cheaply; the charge guard protects money directly. The scheduler guard as described ("same local date and same cron match") would also suppress legitimate repeat jobs and is stored only in memory, so its exact semantics need confirming.

reconstruction.problem: On 25 Oct, Europe/Berlin clocks went back, so local 02:30 occurred twice. The scheduler fired charge_renewals at 00:30Z and again at 01:30:02Z, and send_dunning also ran twice. The 212 renewing subscriptions were selected twice because renews_on is only advanced later by settle_renewals at 04:00Z, and psp.charge sends no idempotency key to Payrail.
reconstruction.what_breaks: 212 subscribers were charged twice, 41 duplicate dunning emails were sent, and settle_renewals reported settled=424. Support refunded some customers by hand on 26 Oct and kept no list (KB-519), so the remaining affected customers are unidentified.
reconstruction.fix: Two guards: (1) in scheduler/clock.py due_jobs, skip a job whose last fire has the same local date and cron match, with loop.py storing the date in last_fired; (2) in billing/renewals.py add AND NOT EXISTS on renewal_charges for the same subscription and charged_on date. Alternatives: set charge_renewals to timezone UTC as a one-line hotfix, or send a Payrail idempotency key (unverified that Payrail supports one).
reconstruction.cost: Both code changes are described as small. Limits: last_fired is in memory so a restart loses it (only the charge guard covers that); on spring-forward night the 02:30 job is skipped that day but runs the next day; the UTC alternative does not protect send_dunning or other local-time jobs; neither guard covers a crash between psp.charge and the renewal_charges insert.

follow_up_questions: Does the charge guard's charged_on date use the same local-vs-UTC date basis in both the insert and the query, so it can't misfire around midnight or the DST shift?
Is the scheduler guard keyed per job and per cron match, so that a job legitimately scheduled multiple times a day is not suppressed?
Is the renewal_charges insert atomic with psp.charge, or can a crash between them leave a charged subscription unrecorded?
reader.closing_answer: Yes, I approve both guards. Ship the charge_renewals NOT EXISTS check first, then the scheduler dedupe once you confirm it is keyed per job and cron match. Also apply the UTC change to charge_renewals as an immediate hotfix if the code can't land quickly. Then start on identifying the remaining double-charged customers: compare the duplicate renewal_charges rows for 25 Oct with the refunds support issued.
